title: Decision Trees — A Staircase Approximation
key_insight: This makes trees flexible but discontinuous: a tiny move across a split can jump the prediction. Oblique trees use angled cuts, while ordinary trees cut one feature at a time.
body:
## A Staircase Approximation

A smooth landscape is covered with rectangular steps. Each leaf is one flat rectangle, so a deeper tree can trace a more detailed staircase.

This makes trees flexible but discontinuous: a tiny move across a split can jump the prediction. Oblique trees use angled cuts, while ordinary trees cut one feature at a time.

Exact best-tree search grows too quickly to try fully, so libraries use greedy building plus pruning. Fast implementations sort values and reuse split statistics.
common_mistakes: Growing until every training row has its own leaf.
Reading one greedy split as the only valid explanation.
Ignoring the advantage given to features with many possible cut points.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “A Staircase Approximation” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Trees handle curved rules and mixed features while remaining inspectable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “A Staircase Approximation” story, explain Decision Trees without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
